title: PokeTool
tagline: A Unity editor tool to browse, create and edit the game's content, built with UI Toolkit and documented design decisions.
overview: An editor window for Unity 6 that lets you view, create and edit the content of [Pokémon Battle Clone](#pokemon-battle-clone): Pokémon, moves and teams, all stored as ScriptableObjects. It opens from the `PokeTool/Open` menu.
It was my way of learning **UI Toolkit and Addressables from scratch** while building something with real technical substance.

highlights.title: Three browsers
highlights.text: Pokémon, Moves and Teams tabs, each with search, toolbar and creation popups.

highlights.title: PokeAPI import
highlights.text: Loads base stats, types and sprites straight into ScriptableObjects.

highlights.title: Team editor
highlights.text: Up to 6 members with rich search rows, level, nature, EVs, IVs and final stats shown as bars, plus Undo/Redo.

highlights.title: Addressable sprites
highlights.text: Sprites are loaded by ID convention instead of being referenced directly by the configs.

decisions.title: Composition over inheritance
decisions.text: When two types share little, a small duplicated class is fine. When they share a lot, it generalizes with `Foo<T>` that receives what is specific through a delegate or constructor (`ConfigRepository<T>`, `ConfigBrowser<T>`, `ConfigPicker<T>`).

decisions.title: Functions instead of repositories in the UI
decisions.text: UI classes receive things like `Func<List<T>>` or `Func<T, Sprite>`, so they stay small and easy to reason about.

decisions.title: Typed UI rows
decisions.text: Each row is its own class with typed references and a `Bind(...)` method, instead of string-based queries scattered around.

decisions.title: Hand-wired composition root
decisions.text: No DI container: the tool is small enough that explicit wiring is clearer.

decisions.title: A cleaner stats domain
decisions.text: A `Stat` enum, an immutable `StatSet`, `StatsData` and `Nature` give a single source of names and limits.

decisions.title: Reserved ID range for custom content
decisions.text: IDs from 11000 are reserved for custom content, so it never collides with PokeAPI IDs.

decisions.title: Decisions written down with their why
decisions.text: For example, closing the detail panel on Undo because of stale cached state in the pickers, or replacing drag-and-drop with arrows.

limitations: Deleting a move or Pokémon referenced by a team is not handled yet (the plan is to block deletion when in use).
learnings: UI Toolkit and Addressables, learned by building a tool with a real use.
Designing editor tooling around workflows and decisions, not just features.
